original_question: Let G be a graph that admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time tau, meaning that all entries of the mixing matrix M(t) = U(t) o U(-t) are equal at t = tau, or equivalently that all entries of U(tau) = exp(i tau A) have the same absolute value. Prove that every eigenvalue of U(tau) is a root of unity.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open Problem 3.1: 'Show that if G admits uniform mixing at time τ, then the eigenvalues of U(τ) are roots of unity, or find a counter-example.'
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant part of the paper: it uses the paper’s continuous-time quantum walk notation U(t)=exp(itA), the mixing matrix M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t), and the paper’s equivalent description of instantaneous uniform mixing as 'all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value.' missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem, not as an established theorem to prove unconditionally.
The official formulation includes the alternative: 'or find a counter-example.'
The stand-alone statement should specify that G is a graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A.
The definition of uniform mixing in the paper is that all entries of M(τ) are equal, in fact equal to 1/n; your draft says 'equal' but does not mention the explicit value 1/n.
The paper’s official formulation uses the phrase 'admits uniform mixing at time τ'; the stand-alone version should define this before asking the question.
The question should make clear that U(t) is the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on G.
The problem should stay narrowly scoped to the root-of-unity conclusion and not turn into a broader classification or characterization problem.
refined_question: Let G be a graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A, and let U(t)=exp(itA) be the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on G. Define the mixing matrix by M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t). Say that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time τ if all entries of M(τ) are equal (equivalently, all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value). Show that if G admits uniform mixing at time τ, then every eigenvalue of U(τ) is a root of unity, or else give a counterexample.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent hypothesis only: G admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time τ iff all entries of M(τ) are equal, particularly to 1/n, iff all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value.
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the paper’s uniform-mixing root-of-unity problem. The exact nearest formulation is Open Problem 3.1 in Section 3, page 6. The nearby text on page 6 supplies the needed definitions of U(t), M(t), and 'uniform mixing,' including the equivalence between equal entries of M(τ) and equal absolute values of entries of U(τ). The main paper-faithful correction is that the paper does not ask only for a proof; it asks to prove the claim or find a counterexample. The explicit value 1/n for the entries of M(τ) is also part of the paper’s definition and makes the question fully stand-alone.
